chapter: Purple Derby Orchestra on the Gulf Coast
title: Purple Derby Orchestra members and instrumentation
summary: Looking at a photo of the eight-man orchestra, they name members such as Joe Mitchell and Ed Powers on tenor; Lizana played alto and soprano.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played what: early band size and instrumentation

blocks.x: Well, what would your special derby orchestra be?
There was jazz band. There was jazz band.
There was jazz band. There was jazz band. Tell me a little bit more about it. I see you got some men in here. You got all kind of instruments.
Yeah.
In the pictures.

Well, that little orchestra there I believe had more. I know mine. I've never played any orchestra and had as many pieces as that thing. We had a lot of music. How many men I got? Eight men I believe in it.

Yeah, it's eight men in this picture. And I can see two cornets, a banjo, two fiddles, drums, alto, tenor, soprano. Two paronets, one's an outlet system and one's a bane system. And a tuba in here. No trombone, huh?
No, I believe we took two fiddles instead of the trombone. We took an extra fiddle. Yeah.
And it says on the back, the XANA director, Tuva Gerard Levison, is that his name? Who?
Levy. Oh, Levy? Leviton. Leviton, that's right.
Gerard Levison. Other members, Debbie P. Finkel. Who is Debbie P. Finkel?
Little Finkel. What did he put in here? I know him very well. I was trying to keep an instant take him.
But I think we got it all in here somewhere, aren't we?
Yeah. Remember the battery, not Mitchell? Probably.
Well, Joe Mitchell? Remember him? Yeah. Who is he?
I'll have to look at the van. Mm-hmm. Well, you don't have the instruments there, you know. No. No. Shane Martin. Is that Shane Martin? No, Shane Martin. Shane. I think, uh... I don't know.
So they got Joe Mitchell, Bob Robinson, Victor Corsi.
I think that's Joe Mitchell, if I'm not mistaken. He played Gana. And he also played Sticks. Marimba. Marimba. Marimba.
Bob Robinson, Joe Waddle, and Edward J. Powers, the sax wizard.
Yep.
Yep.
Yeah. You know, you get his horn. See, the horn, I mean, it's really right. Yeah. Well, what... Ed Powers was a guest. Yeah. He was a guest. I see.
And he... What's... You said you were playing the soprano and alto, so... Yeah. What instrument did he play?
Ed Powers played the tenor.
Mm-hmm.
I played the alto and the soprano, and Ed Powers played the tenor.

I guess he must have been playing the Albert system. He was. Yeah. Because it shows in the picture, one Albert and one Bane system. Well, anyway, where did y'all play? I see in the Scrab Bucket's got the Ratskeller there. What was that?
